data.title: Ciclopirox olamine (1% cream, 8% nail lacquer)
data.body:
_Topicals · I Antifungals — Other_

**Class:** Hydroxypyridone antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Chelates trivalent metal ions (Fe³⁺, Al³⁺) → inhibits metal-dependent enzymes (catalase, peroxidase, cytochromes) needed for fungal metabolism
- Different from azoles and allylamines — no cross-resistance
- Broad spectrum: dermatophytes, Candida, Malassezia, non-dermatophyte moulds, Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria; anti-inflammatory

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 1% cream/gel: tinea, candidiasis, pityriasis versicolor, seborrhoeic dermatitis
- 1% shampoo: seborrhoeic dermatitis of scalp
- 8% nail lacquer: mild–moderate onychomycosis without matrix involvement (also in children), and as adjunct to oral therapy

## Dose & formulations
- Cream: twice daily for 2–4 weeks
- Lacquer: apply daily to the nail and 5 mm of surrounding skin; apply new layers over old; remove all layers weekly with alcohol; trim/file the nail; continue up to 48 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Cream: mild burning, itching
- Lacquer: periungual redness, nail discolouration, ingrown nail (rare)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; avoid unless needed.

## Viva points
- Metal chelator — unique mechanism
- 8% lacquer daily; remove weekly with alcohol; 48 weeks
- Antifungal + antibacterial + anti-inflammatory

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.42; Khopkar ch.19. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
